How Signals Work

RapidSift evaluates each ticker against multiple independent strategies every cycle. When a strategy's conditions are met, a buy or sell signal fires. A 5-day cooldown prevents the same strategy from re-firing on the same ticker within 5 trading days. When 2 or more buy signals fire on the same ticker on the same day, a Confluence signal is also generated.

RSI RSI (Relative Strength Index) Buy + Sell

Measures momentum by comparing the magnitude of recent gains to recent losses over a rolling window. When RSI crosses below the oversold threshold, a buy signal fires. When it crosses above the overbought threshold, a sell signal fires. Only fires on the transition day.

Period 14
Oversold ≤ 30
Overbought ≥ 70
Cooldown 5d
MACD MACD Crossover Buy + Sell

Tracks the relationship between two exponential moving averages. When the MACD line crosses above the signal line → buy. When it crosses below → sell.

Fast EMA 12
Slow EMA 26
Signal EMA 9
Cooldown 5d
MA CROSS Moving Average Crossover Buy + Sell

When the fast SMA crosses above the slow SMA → buy. Crossing below → sell.

Fast SMA 20
Slow SMA 50
Cooldown 5d
VOL SPIKE Volume Spike Buy + Sell

Detects abnormally high volume vs 20-day average. Down day + spike → buy. Up day + spike → sell.

Multiplier 2.0x
Lookback 20 days
Cooldown 5d
PCT CHG Percent Change (Volatility-Normalized) Buy + Sell

Fires when a single-day move exceeds N standard deviations of trailing 20-day returns. Big drop → buy. Big surge → sell.

Sigma 2.0σ
Lookback 20 days
Fallback 3.0%
Cooldown 5d
ADJ DROP Market-Adjusted Drop Buy only

Stock return minus SPY return. When adjusted return crosses below threshold → buy.

Threshold -5.0%
Benchmark SPY
Cooldown 5d
ADJ SURGE Market-Adjusted Surge Sell only

Inverse of adjusted drop. When adjusted return exceeds threshold → sell.

Threshold +5.0%
Benchmark SPY
Cooldown 5d
THRESHOLD Price Threshold Buy + Sell

User-defined price alerts per ticker.

Rules Custom per ticker
CONFLUENCE Confluence (Composite) Buy only

Not an independent strategy — fires automatically when 2 or more buy signals trigger on the same ticker on the same day. The idea is that multiple indicators agreeing simultaneously is a stronger signal than any one alone. Tracked and validated separately so you can compare its win rate against individual strategies.

Min signals 2
Validation

Each buy signal is validated by checking whether the price hit the gain target (+5% or +10%) within 14 trading days. Entry price is the next trading day's open after the signal fires, not the signal-day close. The market benchmark for adjusted returns is SPY (S&P 500 ETF). Win rates on the Reliability tab compare each strategy against a random-entry baseline to show real edge.
